## Build the sentence

::: {.sentence-builder}
- The Romans / built / long, straight roads. ![](images/via-appia.jpg)
- Aqueducts / carried / water / to the city. ![](images/pont-du-gard.jpg)
- Augustus / was / the first emperor / of Rome. ![](images/augustus-prima-porta.jpg)
- Gladiators / fought / in the Colosseum. ![](images/colosseum-forum.jpg)
- The Senate / gave / advice / to the consuls. | Who gave advice?
:::

::: notes
Students drag the words into order (or tap them in order). **Check** turns the words in the right place green and the others red. Then **Next sentence**.

To make your own: a `::: {.sentence-builder}` list, one sentence each. The words are mixed up for you. Use `/` to keep words together as one tile ("long, straight roads"); without `/`, every word is its own tile. The full stop stays at the end. Add a picture, or a hint after a `|`.
:::

## Fill in the blanks

::: {.fill-blanks extra="soldiers, temples"}
The Romans needed lots of clean [water] for their cities. They built [aqueducts] to carry it from the mountains.

The water flowed down a gentle [slope], so they needed no pumps. Many aqueducts went over valleys on tall [arches].
:::

::: notes
Students drag each word from the word bank into its gap (or tap a word, then a gap). Tap a filled gap to take its word out. **Check** marks each gap green or red.

To make your own: write the text, with each missing word in `[square brackets]`. The word bank is made from them. `extra="soldiers, temples"` adds wrong words to the bank, so it's harder.
:::

## How to build a Roman road

::: {.put-in-order}
- Dig a deep trench. | First, the workers dug down about a meter.
- Fill it with big stones. | Big stones made a strong base.
- Add small stones and sand. | Smaller stones filled the gaps.
- Put flat stones on top. | Flat stones made a smooth surface.
- Make the middle a little higher. | Rain ran off to the sides.
:::

::: notes
Students drag the cards into order (or tap one card, then the place it goes). **Check** turns the cards in the right place green. When they're all right, the reasons show.

To make your own: a `::: {.put-in-order}` list in the **right** order; the cards are mixed up for you. A reason after a `|` is optional. When every card has a picture, the cards sit side by side (next slide). `first="Oldest" last="Newest"` changes the words at the ends.
:::

## Greece, Rome, or both?

::: {.sort layout="venn"}
- **Ancient Greece**
  - The first democracy | Athens had the first democracy.
  - The Olympic Games | The first Olympic Games were in Greece.
  - City-states | Greece was many city-states, not one country.
- **Both**
  - Many gods | Greeks and Romans both prayed to many gods.
  - Temples with columns | Both built temples with tall columns.
  - Theaters and plays | Both watched plays in big theaters.
- **Ancient Rome**
  - Emperors | Rome had emperors, like Augustus.
  - Aqueducts | The Romans built aqueducts to carry water.
  - Latin | The Romans spoke Latin. The Greeks spoke Greek.
:::

::: notes
A Sort it with `layout="venn"`: exactly three groups, in the order left circle, middle ("both"), right circle. Students tap an item, then a part of the diagram. A wrong one shakes and shows the reason after the `|`.
:::
